recorded_at: after the quorum round and the correction it produced

quorum.rounds: one round of three sandboxed lanes on 691c1faa with the base pinned at d7028f5b: 0/3 PASS. The brief forbade judging a data change from a summary: every lane parsed both versions of the roadmap into structured rows and diffed them field by field, ran the refused pmat transition itself, and read the receipt as a hostile reader.
quorum.kill_rule: nine claims survived three independent parses of the file; the tenth did not. The refutation was corrected in the tree rather than argued, and no second round was run because three lanes had already produced the right figures from the data itself.
refuted_claims: As worded: '183 rows before, 183 after, none lost or added' — refuted 3/3. The file holds 184 rows at the base and 186 at HEAD; the two added are PMAT-235 and PMAT-236, minted on this branch. The figure was true of the measurement taken and false of the commit, because it was taken before those rows existed, and the count also used a PMAT- regex that missed the one row whose id does not begin with PMAT-. Corrected in the receipt and the log, with the reason.

falsification.not_applicable: this branch contains no code: the diff is the roadmap's status field, a receipt and one audit log. There is no test to revert and none was run. What stands in place of a falsifier is that the change was made by a tool that refuses an illegal transition rather than by editing YAML, and that three independent lanes parsed both versions of the file field by field and found one error, which is corrected.

crux.verdict: accept(docs/audits/crux-1.28.0.md row 1 surveyed how these projects link work to the release that carries it and found every one of them recording the link at merge and reconciling it at the cut. None of them keeps a second, hand-maintained status field beside that link, which is exactly the field that drifted here: the machine-checked half was right for five releases while the human-read half was wrong. The fix files the missing check rather than adding a second source of truth.)
